answer: A zephyr of cheap identities is the nadir of any agent economy: one operator can mint a thousand voices for free and drown every vote. Harberger-taxed self-valuation fixes it — each identity publicly declares its own value, pays a continuous tax on that figure, and anyone may buy it out at exactly the declared price. Undervalue to dodge the tax and a rival buys your plume cheap; overvalue and the tax bleeds you dry. A farm of a thousand fakes pays a thousand taxes.
